reply.english: Yes, I'll bring it for you.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Welcome. How can I help you?

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: I want a shirt for work.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: What's your size?

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: I don't know. I think it's medium.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Here you are, this is a nice shirt.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: Is this fabric cotton?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Yes, pure cotton.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: Can I try it on?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Of course. The fitting room is on the right.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: هَذَا كَبِيرٌ عَلَيَّ. هَلْ يُوجَدُ مَقَاسٌ أَصْغَر؟
dialogue.transliteration: haadhaa kabeerun 3alayya. hal yoojadu maqaasun asghar?
dialogue.english: This is too big for me. Do you have a smaller size?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Yes, I'll bring it for you.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.transliteration: jarrabtuhu wa huwa munaasibun lee. sa2aakhudhuhu.
dialogue.english: I tried it on and it fits me. I'll take it.

response.english: Yes, the fitting room is over there.

pair.english: This is too big for me.

response.english: I'll bring you a smaller size.

lessons.culture: In shops the seller often asks مَا مَقَاسُكَ؟ first, and a polite customer asks هَلْ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُجَرِّبَهُ؟ before buying. Sizes are usually given as letters such as S, M and L, or as European numbers.

exercises.prompt: The seller asks you: 'مَا مَقَاسُكَ؟'. Say your size is medium.
exercises.tip: مُتَوَسِّط means 'medium'; the ending ـِي on مَقَاسِي means 'my'.

exercises.prompt: You try a shirt on and it is too big. Tell the seller.
exercises.tip: عَلَيَّ here means 'on me', so 'too big for me'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'هَلْ _____ مَقَاسٌ أَصْغَر؟' (Do you have a smaller size?)
exercises.tip: هَلْ يُوجَدُ is the formal way to ask 'is there'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'أُرِيدُ _____ رِيَاضِيًّا.' (I want sports shoes.)
exercises.tip: حِذَاء means 'a shoe'; رِيَاضِيّ describes it as 'sports'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'I want a dress.'
exercises.tip: أُرِيدُ is 'I want'; the thing wanted follows it.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Where's the fitting room?'
exercises.tip: غُرْفَةُ الْقِيَاس is literally 'the measuring room'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'I tried it on and it fits me.'
exercises.tip: جَرَّبْتُ is 'I tried'; the ending ـهُ is 'it'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'This is too tight for me'?
exercises.tip: ضَيِّق is 'tight'; كَبِير is 'big'.

exercises.prompt: Which question asks a woman her size?
exercises.tip: The ending كِ speaks to a woman; كَ to a man.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'أَصْغَر؟ / مَقَاسٌ / يُوجَدُ / هَلْ'.
exercises.tip: The question starts with هَلْ and the size comes last.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'رِيَاضِيًّا / حِذَاءً / أُرِيدُ'.
exercises.tip: The describing word رِيَاضِيًّا follows the noun.

reply.english: Yes, we have red and black.

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.english: What do you think of this dress?

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: جَمِيلٌ جِدًّا، وَهُوَ مِنْ أَحْدَثِ مَا عِنْدَنَا.
dialogue.transliteration: jameelun jiddan, wa huwa min a7dathi maa 3indanaa.
dialogue.english: Very beautiful, and it is one of our newest.

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.arabic: يُعْجِبُنِي اللَّوْنُ الْأَزْرَق، لَكِنَّهُ دَاكِنٌ جِدًّا عَلَيَّ.
dialogue.transliteration: yu3jibunee al-lawnu al-azraq, lakinnahu daakinun jiddan 3alayya.
dialogue.english: I like the blue color, but it is too dark for me.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.english: Do you like light colors?

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، أُحِبُّهَا. هَلْ يُوجَدُ لَوْنٌ آخَر؟
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, u7ibbuhaa. hal yoojadu lawnun aakhar?
dialogue.english: Yes, I like them. Do you have another color?

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.english: We have green and white.

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.english: Which is nicer, green or white?

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.english: The white is nicer than the green.

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.english: The green doesn't suit me. What do you recommend?

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.english: Choose this white one, it suits you.

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.arabic: لَمْ أُقَرِّرْ بَعْد. هَلْ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُفَكِّرَ قَلِيلًا؟
dialogue.transliteration: lam uqarrir ba3d. hal astatee3u an ufakkira qaleelan?
dialogue.english: I haven't decided yet. Can I think for a little while?

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.english: Of course, take your time.

response.english: Yes, we have red and black.

pair.english: What do you think of this dress?

response.english: This one is nicer than that one.

lessons.culture: Sellers like to ask مَا رَأْيُكَ؟ and to suggest a color, and it is polite to say يُعْجِبُنِي before you say what you dislike. Saying لَمْ أُقَرِّرْ بَعْد is an easy way to keep looking without buying.

exercises.prompt: The seller asks: 'مَا رَأْيُكَ فِي هَذَا الْفُسْتَان؟'. Say you like the blue color.
exercises.tip: يُعْجِبُنِي means 'it pleases me', the usual way to say 'I like'.

exercises.prompt: The seller asks: 'هَلْ اخْتَرْتَ؟' (Have you chosen?). Say you haven't decided yet.
exercises.tip: لَمْ before a present verb gives the past negative.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'هَذَا _____ مِنْ ذَلِكَ.' (This one is nicer than that one.)
exercises.tip: أَجْمَلُ is 'nicer'; مِنْ gives 'than'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'هَذَا اللَّوْنُ لَا _____.' (This color doesn't suit me.)
exercises.tip: يُنَاسِبُ is 'suits'; ـنِي is 'me'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Do you have another color?'
exercises.tip: آخَر means 'another' and follows the noun.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'I like light colors.'
exercises.tip: فَاتِح is 'light'; دَاكِن is 'dark'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Just give me this one.'
exercises.tip: فَقَط means 'only' and softens the request.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'gray'?
exercises.tip: رَمَاد is 'ash', so the color is ash-colored.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'This is too dark for me'?
exercises.tip: جِدًّا means 'very' or 'too'.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'الْأَزْرَق؟ / أَمِ / الْأَحْمَرُ / أَجْمَلُ، / أَيُّهُمَا'.
exercises.tip: أَمِ joins the two choices.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'ذَلِكَ / مِنْ / أَجْمَلُ / هَذَا'.
exercises.tip: مِنْ comes before the thing compared.

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.english: How much is this shirt?

dialogue.speaker: Adel
dialogue.english: For a hundred dinars.

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.arabic: هَذَا غَالٍ جِدًّا. هَلْ يُمْكِنُكَ تَخْفِيضُ السِّعْر؟
dialogue.transliteration: haadhaa ghaalin jiddan. hal yumkinuka takhfeedu as-si3r?
dialogue.english: That's very expensive. Can you lower the price?

dialogue.speaker: Adel
dialogue.english: How much do you want to pay?

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.english: Take it for seventy.

dialogue.speaker: Adel

dialogue.transliteration: laa astatee3u, sa2akhsar. haadhaa aakhiru si3r: thamaanoona deenaaran.
dialogue.english: I can't, I'll lose money. This is the final price: eighty dinars.

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.english: Isn't there anything cheaper than this?

dialogue.speaker: Adel
dialogue.english: I have this one for fifty dinars.

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.arabic: أُرِيدُ خَصْمًا لِأَنَّنِي أَشْتَرِي كَثِيرًا. سَآخُذُ ثَلَاثَةَ قُمْصَان.
dialogue.transliteration: ureedu khasman li2annanee ashtaree katheeran. sa2aakhudhu thalaathata qumsaan.
dialogue.english: I want a discount because I'm buying a lot. I'll take three shirts.

dialogue.speaker: Adel
dialogue.english: Fine, take them for a hundred and thirty.

dialogue.speaker: Samir
dialogue.english: We agreed. How much did the total come to?

dialogue.speaker: Adel
dialogue.english: A hundred and thirty dinars. Here you are.

response.english: Here you are, this is yours.

lessons.culture: Bargaining is expected in markets and small shops but not in big stores with fixed prices. A calm, friendly tone matters more than the number, and اِتَّفَقْنَا closes the deal.

exercises.prompt: You want to know the price of a bag. What do you ask?
exercises.tip: بِكَمْ is 'for how much'.

exercises.prompt: The seller says: 'هَذَا آخِرُ سِعْر'. You agree.
exercises.tip: اِتَّفَقْنَا means 'we agreed'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'هَذَا _____ جِدًّا.' (It's very expensive.)
exercises.tip: غَالٍ is 'expensive' (dear).

exercises.prompt: Complete: '_____ لِي السِّعْرَ قَلِيلًا.' (Lower the price a bit for me.)
exercises.tip: خَفِّضْ is the command 'lower', said to one man.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Isn't there cheaper than this?'
exercises.tip: أَرْخَصُ is 'cheaper'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'I can't, I'll lose money.'
exercises.tip: سَـ before a verb makes it future.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'How much did the total come to?'
exercises.tip: بَلَغَ means 'reached'.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase closes a deal?
exercises.tip: It means 'we have agreed'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'I want a discount because I'm buying a lot'?

exercises.tip: لِأَنَّنِي means 'because I'.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'السِّعْر؟ / تَخْفِيضُ / يُمْكِنُكَ / هَلْ'.
exercises.tip: يُمْكِنُكَ means 'it is possible for you'.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'بِأَلْفَيْن / خُذْهُ'.
exercises.tip: أَلْفَيْن is 'two thousand'.

dialogue.speaker: Nadia
dialogue.english: Hello. I want to return this shirt.

dialogue.speaker: Hani
dialogue.english: Welcome. What's the problem?

dialogue.speaker: Nadia
dialogue.english: There's a defect, here at the sleeve.

dialogue.speaker: Hani
dialogue.english: Sorry. When did you buy it?

dialogue.speaker: Nadia
dialogue.english: I bought it yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: Hani
dialogue.english: Do you have the receipt?

dialogue.speaker: Nadia
dialogue.english: Yes, I have the receipt. Here you are.

dialogue.speaker: Hani
dialogue.english: Do you want to exchange it for another one?

dialogue.speaker: Nadia
dialogue.arabic: لَا، لَمْ يُعْجِبْنِي اللَّوْن أَيْضًا. هَلْ تُعِيدُونَ الْمَال؟
dialogue.transliteration: laa, lam yu3jibnee al-lawn aydan. hal tu3eedoona al-maal?
dialogue.english: No, I didn't like the color either. Do you give money back?

dialogue.speaker: Hani
dialogue.english: Yes, we give the money back within a week.

dialogue.speaker: Nadia
dialogue.english: Good. Thanks for your cooperation.

dialogue.speaker: Hani
dialogue.english: You're welcome. We hope to see you soon.

response.english: Do you want to exchange it?

lessons.culture: Most shops accept a return with the receipt within a week or two, and staff usually offer an exchange before a refund. End with شُكْرًا عَلَى تَعَاوُنِكُمْ, where the plural form is polite to the whole shop.

exercises.prompt: The seller asks: 'هَلْ مَعَكَ الْفَاتُورَة؟'. Say you have it.
exercises.tip: مَعِي means 'with me'.

exercises.prompt: The seller asks: 'مَتَى اشْتَرَيْتَهُ؟'. Say you bought it yesterday.
exercises.tip: The ending تُ is 'I' and هُ is 'it'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'فِيهِ _____.' (There's a defect.)
exercises.tip: عَيْب means a fault or defect.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'هَذَا لَيْسَ _____ الصَّحِيح.' (This is the wrong size.)
exercises.tip: After لَيْسَ the word takes the ending ـَ.

exercises.tip: إِرْجَاع is 'returning'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'I don't have the receipt.'
exercises.tip: لَيْسَ is the word for 'is not'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Can I exchange it for a bigger size?'
exercises.tip: بِ after اسْتِبْدَال gives 'for'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'This isn't what I ordered'?
exercises.tip: مَا طَلَبْتُهُ is 'what I ordered'.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'receipt'?
exercises.tip: فَاتُورَة is the word for a bill or receipt.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'بِآخَر / اسْتِبْدَالَهُ / أُرِيدُ'.
exercises.tip: بِآخَر means 'for another'.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'الْمَال؟ / تُعِيدُونَ / هَلْ'.
exercises.tip: تُعِيدُونَ is 'you give back' (plural, polite).

challenge.title: Buy a shirt and bring it back
challenge.instructions: Write a short conversation in Fusha between a customer and a seller. The customer asks for a shirt, says the size, tries it on, chooses a color, bargains over the price, agrees, and the next day comes back to exchange it.
required_elements: asking for an item and giving a size
trying it on and saying if it fits
returning or exchanging with a reason and the receipt

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Welcome. How can I help you?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: أُرِيدُ قَمِيصًا. هَلْ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُجَرِّبَهُ؟

dialogue.speaker: Omar

dialogue.speaker: Rami

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: For fifty dinars.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: هَذَا غَالٍ جِدًّا. خَفِّضْ لِي السِّعْرَ قَلِيلًا.

dialogue.english: That's very expensive. Lower the price a bit for me.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: This is the final price: forty dinars.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: Ok, we agreed.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: مَرْحَبًا مَرَّةً أُخْرَى. هَذَا لَيْسَ الْمَقَاسَ الصَّحِيح. مَعِي الْفَاتُورَة.

dialogue.english: Hello again. This is the wrong size. I have the receipt.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: لَا بَأْس. هَلْ تُرِيدُ اسْتِبْدَالَهُ بِمَقَاسٍ أَكْبَر؟ شُكْرًا عَلَى تَعَاوُنِكَ.
dialogue.transliteration: laa ba2s. hal tureedu istibdaalahu bimaqaasin akbar? shukran 3alaa ta3aawunika.
dialogue.english: No problem. Do you want to exchange it for a bigger size? Thanks for your cooperation.
